data.title: Cathie Wood Says TSLA Holders ‘Will Get’ A Premium If SpaceX Buys Tesla — HSBC Puts It At Over 30%
data.description:
Key points:
  • HSBC models a 33% premium, valuing Tesla at $507 a share in a deal or $212 on its own.
  • Wood sees Tesla’s robotaxis helping fund SpaceX’s orbital data centers.
  • A deal could reportedly be announced in December and would need backing from holders of 50% of Tesla shares.

If SpaceX wants Tesla shareholders to approve a buyout, ARK Investment Management CEO Cathie Wood believes it will have to offer them a premium, and HSBC estimates that a bid 33% above Tesla’s 30-day average would value the stock at $507 per share.

“We do think the Tesla shareholder will demand a premium and will get a premium, whether it’s going to be 25% or what have you. I think it’s going to be worth it to SpaceX,” Wood told CNBC’s Squawk Box on Friday.

While neither company has announced an offer, Tesla shareholders would have considerable say over any deal. Elon Musk told investors in October that a merger would need the backing of holders of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares. Even a majority of the votes cast could fall short.

HSBC Puts Tesla Buyout At $507 Per Share 

The prospect of a SpaceX bid changed how HSBC values Tesla stock. “Given the acquisition newsflow, we believe the current share price of Tesla offers an anchor, irrespective of the fundamentals,” the bank said in a note.

Drawing on premiums paid in comparable deals, HSBC estimated that a bid 33% above Tesla’s 30-day average would value the stock at $507 a share. If Tesla stays independent, the bank values it at $212 a share based on the cash it expects Tesla’s seven businesses to generate. HSBC gave the two outcomes equal weight and more than doubled its price target to $359 from $157, implying a 4% upside from current levels, while upgrading the stock to ‘Hold’ from ‘Reduce.’

Wood Makes The Case For A Tesla Premium 

Meanwhile, Wood sees a role for Tesla’s robotaxis in one of SpaceX’s most expensive ambitions. “In the short-term, RoboTaxi is going to deliver massive cash flows, we believe, which will help fund orbital data centers,” she said. Wood expects computing in orbit to become cheaper than computing on Earth within two years. In a stock-for-stock deal, Tesla investors would own a piece of the business their robotaxis could help finance.

ARK owns both stocks and has run the numbers from each side of the table. In October, its researchers estimated that a premium of about 24% to Tesla’s closing price at the time would divide the projected gains from a merger evenly between the two groups of shareholders.

The companies already have an elaborate business relationship. Tesla booked $626 million in revenue from sales of its Megapack batteries to SpaceX in the first nine months of 2026. Additionally, billionaire investor Chamath Palihapitiya sees a broader opportunity in bringing their power supplies, chips, AI models, and products under one roof. At SpaceX’s Starbase in Texas, Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas flagged a computing campus of more than one gigawatt, according to a note shared by Tesla investor Sawyer Merritt.

HSBC Sees Control As Musk’s Main Motive 

HSBC also sees a clear incentive for Musk in a potential merger. SpaceX’s share structure gives him more voting power than he has at Tesla. “We see control as the key motivation for a merger, especially as CEO Musk has been clear in the past about his need for oversight,” the bank said.

Independent directors at both companies are weighing a possible deal. Musk said his role at each company keeps him out of those talks. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he told investors on SpaceX’s earnings call last month. SpaceX and Tesla could reportedly announce a merger as early as December, though the announcement could slip into early 2027.

Baron Sees Gains With Or Without A Merger 

On the other hand, Ron Baron, a longtime shareholder in both Tesla and SpaceX, declined to say what price would win his vote. “Whatever their decision is, I’m going to support him,” Baron said in a CNBC interview.

Baron said his investments in Musk’s companies had already earned about $30 billion and could generate hundreds of billions more over the next decade. When asked whether the gains depended on Tesla and SpaceX joining forces, he replied, “Doesn’t matter to me. He’s going to do what’s best for the companies and for operating most efficiently.”

How Do Retail Traders Feel About TSLA And SPCX?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘neutral’ on Tesla and ‘bearish’ on SpaceX at the time of writing, with ‘low’ message volume for both stocks.

One user said the talks could lift Tesla stock after Friday’s selloff: “SpaceX merger discussions remain a potential game-changing catalyst.”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said that the price should come first. “Tesla needs to determine a fair price for its agreement to the SpaceX merger.”

View this Stocktwits post

So far this year, Tesla shares are down 23%, while SpaceX shares are 5% below their June IPO price.

data.title: ConocoPhillips To Sell Norway Business, Stake In UK Teesside Oil Terminal To Vr Energi
data.description:
HOUSTON (dpa-AFX) - Energy major ConocoPhillips (COP) announced Monday a definitive agreement to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the U.K. Teesside oil terminal to Vr Energi.

The total consideration would be $4.425 billion, less agreed upon adjustments of approximately $0.5 billion as of the January 1, 2026, effective date.

Total consideration is expected to be $3.9 billion, including the remaining 2026 tax liability of approximately $1.4 billion, payable in the first half of 2027, resulting in net cash proceeds of around $2.5 billion.

The deal is expected to close by the end of the first quarter 2027, subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and regulatory conditions.

The sale includes ConocoPhillips Skandinavia AS and ConocoPhillips (U.K.) Teesside Operator Limited, which together hold the company's Norway and Teesside assets and associated decommissioning liabilities.

The Norway business includes ConocoPhillips' interests in producing assets on the Norwegian continental shelf, as well as interests in eight partner-operated fields across the Norwegian Sea and northern North Sea.

In 2025, the Norway business produced around 120 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. The year-end 2025 proved reserves associated with the sale

properties were approximately 221 million barrels of oil equivalent.

At the deal closing, Vr Energi will assume the post-effective date balance sheets of the properties.

ConocoPhillips plans to utilize proceeds for general purposes and for discretionary share repurchases in 2027 to supplement its long-standing commitment of

returning around 45% of cash from operations to shareholders.

Andy O'Brien, president and chief executive officer, said, 'Norway and Teesside are high-quality assets with strong operating histories, and we believe this win-win transaction unlocks value for ConocoPhillips while positioning these assets for continued success under new ownership.'

COP shares closed Friday's regular trading on the NYSE at $136.12, up 0.84%, while it lost 0.82% in the after-hours activity.

data.title: Bureau Veritas Acquires Topo Solutions; Strengthens AI-Powered Supply Chain Intelligence Offering
data.description:
PARIS (dpa-AFX) - Bureau Veritas SA (BVI.PA), a France-based testing, inspection and certification services provider, on Monday announced that it has acquired Topo Solutions, an AI-enabled digital supply chain management platform.

The company said that the acquisition will strengthen its AI-powered supply chain intelligence offering.

The deal will also expand its data-driven services and digital solutions for consumer goods companies and retailers worldwide.

The company said that the acquisition is aligned with its LEAP 28 strategy to accelerate growth in strategic markets through bolt-on acquisitions.

Topo Solutions is headquartered in Hong Kong, connects brands and retailers with suppliers, factories and service providers through a single platform.

The company generated approximately 3 million euros in revenue in 2025.

data.title: Smith & Nephew Names Nick Alexos as Next Finance Chief
data.description:
(07:00 GMT) *Smith & Nephew to Appoint Nick Alexos as CFO
(07:02 GMT) *Smith & Nephew: Alexos to Join on Nov. 30
(07:03 GMT) *Smith & Nephew: Alexos Was Most Recently CFO at Univar Solutions
(07:16 GMT) Smith & Nephew Names Nick Alexos as Next Finance Chief

By Adria Calatayud

Smith & Nephew said it would appoint Nick Alexos, a former executive at chemicals distributor Univar Solutions and dental-products supplier Dentsply Sirona, as its next chief financial officer.

The U.K. medical-technology company said Monday that Alexos would join as CFO and board member on Nov. 30.

The company said in August that its previous CFO, John Rogers, would leave at the end of September.

Alexos was most recently CFO at Univar, joining in 2020 when the company was listed on the New York Stock Exchange and staying after Apollo Global took it private in 2023. He was previously CFO and chief administrative officer of Dentsply Sirona between 2017 and 2019.

Smith & Nephew said Alexos would be based in the U.S. and travel widely.

data.title: NQ: Nasdaq Futures Rebound 3% After Brutal Week, Asian Markets Seek Support
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq rebounds after 10% weekly drop
  • Asia equities get government support
  • Gold, Bitcoin rally as dip buyers show up

US futures and gold recover as authorities move to steady Asian stocks. AI financing concerns keep investors cautious.

📈 Futures bounce after a bruising week

  • Nasdaq-100 futures rose 3% in Monday’s Asian session, while S&P 500 futures gained around 2%.
  • Buyers are returning after last week’s rout, although the recovery still leaves substantial losses to repair before sentiment can look more settled.
  • Friday’s cash session explains the scale of that task. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.3%, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Dow lost 1.9%. The Nasdaq suffered its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P and Dow confirmed corrections — declines exceeding 10% from their record closing highs.
  • Anthropic remains a key stock to watch. The newly listed company closed Friday at $88.91, down 8.5%, after touching $83.05, almost its $83 IPO price.

🌏 Asian authorities try to steady stocks

  • Taiwan’s benchmark recovered 2%, while South Korea’s Kospi remained around 2.5% lower after trimming deeper losses. European futures were steady and Japan was closed for a holiday.
  • Policy support is becoming more visible. Taiwan tightened short-selling rules, Chinese exchanges eased margin-financing requirements and South Korea reiterated its readiness to stabilize markets.
  • Those measures may help trading conditions, but investors still need reassurance that enormous AI infrastructure investments can generate adequate returns.
  • The dollar and government bonds largely retained Friday’s defensive gains. The euro remained below $1.10, while USDJPY briefly traded above ¥159.
  • Gold climbed 2.4% to $3,615 after losing about 9% last week, while silver gained 3% to $42.41. Bitcoin traded near $62,000 after touching a one-year low of $55,000 during thin weekend trading.

data.title: Smith+Nephew to appoint Nick Alexos as Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Smith+Nephew (LSE: SN, NYSE: SNN), the global medical technology business, announces Nick Alexos will join the company as Chief Financial Officer and the Board as an Executive Director on 30 November 2026.

Nick brings more than 35 years of financial, commercial and transaction experience, with a strong track record of driving operational performance and creating value from complex situations across global businesses and private equity.

Nick was most recently Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer at Univar Solutions, a global distributor of chemicals and ingredients (2020-2026). He joined Univar Solutions when it was listed on the NYSE (UNVR) and played a central role in delivering the company’s operational transformation. In March 2023, Apollo Global announced it was acquiring Univar Solutions in an $8 billion take-private transaction, which resulted in the Company delisting in 2023. Subsequently Nick continued his work supporting the operational improvement of the business as Chief Financial Officer, and also had responsibility for Univar Solutions’ on-line service business.

Previously, Nick was Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Administrative Officer of dental technology business Dentsply Sirona (2017-2019). As part of a new leadership team, he worked alongside the CEO to reshape the business to improve performance, including programmes focused on capital expenditure, inventory and cost control.

Prior to Dentsply Sirona, Nick spent 30 years at private equity firm Madison Dearborn Partners. As a Managing Director, he co-led 18 platform investments and was responsible for more than $14 billion of debt financings. His portfolio included multiple healthcare investments.

Rupert Soames, Chair of the Board, said: "Nick is an accomplished finance leader with deep experience across global businesses, public markets, private equity and capital markets. His track record in strategic transformation, M&A, financing and disciplined capital allocation will be highly valuable and we look forward to welcoming him to the Board."

Deepak Nath, Chief Executive Officer, said: "I am delighted to welcome Nick to Smith+Nephew. He brings strong financial and commercial leadership and has helped multiple businesses deliver significant value across his career. I look forward to working with him as we continue to sharpen execution, strengthen performance and deliver our strategic priorities."

Nick Alexos said: "I am excited to be joining Smith+Nephew, a global medical technology business with a strong heritage, leading positions in growing markets and significant potential. I look forward to working with Deepak, the Board and colleagues across the company to build on the progress already made and create sustainable value for our stakeholders."

Nick holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and a BBA/CPA in Accounting / Finance from Loyola University, Chicago. He will be based in the United States, but is expected to travel widely.

Investor contacts

Emily Heaven, Smith+Nephew+44 (0) 7811 919437

Media contacts 
Charles Reynolds, Smith+Nephew+44 (0) 1923 477314
Susan Gilchrist / Ayesha Bharmal, Brunswick+44 (0) 20 7404 5959

Remuneration

The Remuneration Committee considered the remuneration arrangements for Nick and agreed the following standard arrangements:

  • Base salary: $900,000 per annum
  • Annual Incentive Plan: Target opportunity of 107.5% of base salary (maximum 215% of base salary)
  • Performance Share Plan: Target opportunity of 150% of base salary (maximum 300% of base salary)
  • Restricted Share Plan: 125% of base salary
  • Shareholding requirement: 300% of base salary
  • Pension and benefits in line with those available to other US employees.

In line with our standard practice for new hires during the year, Nick will also receive a pro-rata 2026 Restricted Share Plan award and a pro-rata 2026-28 Performance Share Plan award.

All arrangements are in line with the approved Director’s Remuneration Policy. Full details will be disclosed in the Directors' Remuneration Report for the relevant year.

There are no further matters required to be disclosed under UKLR 6.4.8R in respect of this appointment.

About Smith+Nephew

Smith+Nephew is a portfolio medical technology business focused on the repair, regeneration and replacement of soft and hard tissue. We exist to restore people’s bodies and their self-belief by using technology to take the limits off living. We call this purpose ‘Life Unlimited’. Our 17,000 employees deliver this mission every day, making a difference to patients’ lives through the excellence of our product portfolio, and the invention and application of new technologies across our three global business units of Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT and Advanced Wound Management.

Founded in Hull, UK, in 1856, we now operate in around 100 countries, and generated annual sales of $6.2 billion in 2025. Smith+Nephew is a constituent of the FTSE100 (LSE:SN, NYSE:SNN). The terms ‘Group’ and ‘Smith+Nephew’ are used to refer to Smith & Nephew plc and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless the context requires otherwise.
